values: register with my email and password
I can create a personal account

• Valid details create a user account
• Duplicate email and invalid inputs are rejected
• Password is stored securely
Implemented by registration validation, ASP.NET Core Identity and confirmation-email dispatch.

• Confirmation token is validated
• Valid token confirms the email
• Invalid or expired token returns a clear error
Implemented by GET /api/auth/confirm-email and Identity email tokens.
I can access my libraries securely

• Valid credentials return authentication tokens
• Invalid credentials do not authenticate
• Protected endpoints require authentication
Implemented by POST /api/auth/login, JWT issuance and protected controllers.
I can continue using the app without repeatedly logging in

• Valid refresh token issues new authentication tokens
• Expired or revoked refresh token is rejected
• Refresh token rotation or revocation is enforced
Implemented by POST /api/auth/refresh with refresh-token rotation and revocation.
I can finish verification when the original message is unavailable

• An unconfirmed account receives a new confirmation challenge
• Confirmed and unknown accounts do not reveal account state
• The endpoint returns a safe, consistent response
log out of my current refresh-token session
a lost token cannot keep creating access tokens

• Logout requires an authenticated user
• The supplied refresh-token session is revoked
• A revoked refresh token cannot be used again
Implemented by POST /api/auth/logout with refresh-session revocation.
receive consistent success and failure responses
the client can handle API outcomes predictably

• Successful responses use the common API envelope
• Validation errors include field-level details
• Authentication, authorization and not-found failures use stable codes and a trace identifier
Implemented by ApiResponse, API behavior configuration and GlobalExceptionMiddleware.
I can keep library information current

• Owner can update the library name
• Invalid names are rejected
• Unauthorized users cannot update it
Implemented by PATCH /api/libraries/{libraryId} with owner/editor authorization.
I can start cataloguing my own collection

• An authenticated user can create a library with a valid name
• Private visibility is used when no visibility is supplied
• The creator is recorded as the Owner member
Implemented by POST /api/libraries with creator ownership.
access only libraries I am authorized to use
other users cannot view or change my collection

• Membership is checked on library-scoped requests
• Non-members cannot read or modify protected data
• Owner role is recorded for the creator
Implemented by library membership checks and owner/editor/viewer enforcement.
books can be associated with their authors

• Author name is required
• Optional biographical fields can be omitted
• Saved author is available for book association

• Publisher name is required
• Website URL is optional
• Saved publisher can be referenced by editions
different editions share the same underlying title

• Title is required
• Optional original title, language, description and first publication year are supported
• Book is stored independently from its editions
Implemented by POST /api/books with work-level metadata.
associate one or more authors with a book

• Existing authors can be linked to a book
• AuthorOrder is retained
• Duplicate book-author associations are prevented
Implemented by ordered BookAuthor associations with duplicate validation.
create an edition for a book
I can distinguish different versions of the same title

• Edition references an existing book
• Publisher is optional
• ISBN-10, ISBN-13, language, date, pages and cover may be omitted
• Multiple editions can belong to one book
Backend implemented by POST /api/book-editions with optional metadata and ISBN validation. The catalogue UI is still required.
I can confirm the correct record before adding it

• Book title and authors are shown
• Available editions and their identifiers are shown
• Optional missing metadata does not break the response
Implemented by book and edition detail endpoints.
add a book copy manually to my library
I can catalogue books even without an ISBN

• User selects or creates the correct book edition
• New copy is associated with the selected library
• Format and reading status have defaults
• Location, condition, acquisition date, price/currency, signed/favourite flags and notes are optional
• Unauthorized users cannot add copies
Backend implemented by POST /api/libraries/{libraryId}/books. The manual-add screen and end-to-end mobile flow are still required.
add multiple copies of the same edition
I can accurately track duplicate physical copies

• Adding an already-owned edition is allowed
• Each copy receives a distinct identifier
• Existing copies are not overwritten
Implemented by distinct BookCopy creation for repeated editions.
view the books in a selected library
I can see what I own

• Only copies from the requested library are returned
• Book title, authors, edition and copy details are available
• Empty library is handled
I can identify a book with minimal typing

• ISBN format and checksum are validated
• Separators may be normalized
• Invalid ISBN receives a useful validation error
Implemented by IsbnNormalizer checksum validation and separator normalization.
look up an ISBN in the local catalogue first
existing data is reused and lookup is fast

• Local editions are searched using normalized ISBN
• Matching local edition is returned without external request
• Missing local edition proceeds to external lookup
Implemented by local-edition lookup before external providers.
retrieve book metadata from Open Library
I can add books without entering every detail

• Open Library lookup is attempted for unknown ISBN
• Found metadata is mapped to a preview
• Not-found and unavailable provider results are handled
Implemented by OpenLibraryMetadataProvider in the provider chain.
receive consistent metadata from different providers
I can review book details in one format

• Provider responses map to Book, Author, Edition and Publisher fields
• Missing values remain optional
• Provider-specific data does not leak into the domain model
Implemented by the common BookMetadata model and provider adapters.
use a fallback metadata provider when the primary source fails
I have a better chance of identifying less common books

• Providers use a common interface
• Next provider is tried on not-found or recoverable failure
• All providers failing returns a clear no-result response
Implemented by FallbackBookMetadataProvider across Google Books, Open Library and web search.
preview identified book information before saving
I can verify the result and avoid incorrect catalogue records

• Preview includes available title, authors, edition and publisher
• Lookup does not create a copy automatically
• User can confirm or cancel
Backend preview is implemented by GET /api/book-metadata/{isbn}; the mobile review and confirmation screen is still required.
be warned if I already own the exact edition
I can avoid accidental duplicate purchases

• ISBN resolves to the edition
• Ownership check is scoped to the selected library
• Response indicates exact-edition ownership and number of copies
Implemented by library-scoped exact-edition ownership checks with copy count.
know if I own a different edition of the same book
I can decide whether I still want another edition

• Other editions are matched through their BookId
• Response distinguishes other-edition ownership from exact match
• Owned edition details are available
see when a book is not owned

• No matching library copy returns not-owned status
• An edition existing globally is not treated as owned
• Result does not expose other libraries’ contents
Implemented by a library-scoped not-owned result without exposing other libraries.
confirm an ISBN lookup and add that edition to my library
the identified book becomes part of my collection

• Existing catalogue entities are reused
• Missing book/edition entities are created when needed
• One new BookCopy is created only after confirmation
• Failure does not leave a partially imported copy
Backend implemented by POST /api/libraries/{libraryId}/book-imports/{isbn}, which resolves catalogue data and creates the copy transactionally. The mobile confirmation flow is still required.
manually complete a book when ISBN lookup fails
books absent from metadata providers can still be catalogued

• No-result response offers manual entry
• Manual entry accepts required fields and optional edition data
• User can save a copy without an ISBN
Manual catalogue and copy APIs support ISBN-free records. The mobile app still needs to detect the final no-result outcome and guide the user through manual entry.

• Registration form validates inputs
• API errors are displayed

log in from the mobile app

• Login form calls the API
• Authenticated state is maintained appropriately
• Invalid credentials show an error
see a home screen with my libraries
I can quickly enter a collection

• Home lists accessible libraries
• User can select a library
• Empty state supports creating a library
I can see my owned books while away from home

• Library screen lists copies/books
• Selecting an item opens its details
• Empty collection displays helpful guidance
scan a book barcode with my phone
I can identify a book without typing its ISBN

• Camera permission is handled
• Readable ISBN barcode is extracted
• Detected ISBN starts lookup or allows confirmation
I can see metadata and ownership before saving

• Lookup screen displays available metadata
• Exact/other/not-owned state is shown
• Add action is offered without forcing it
I can inspect which edition I own

• Book details show authors and edition
• Copy-specific information is visible
• Missing optional metadata is handled
add a book from the mobile app
I can finish cataloguing in one flow

• User can confirm ISBN result or enter details manually
• Selected library receives the new copy
• Success and failure feedback are displayed
I can quickly find a book

• Search is scoped to selected library
• Partial title matches are supported
• No-match state is returned
Library-content searchText supports title matching in the API. The mobile search experience is still required.
I can find all my books by an author

• Author-name matches are supported
• Books with multiple authors are discoverable
• Only accessible library results are returned
I can locate a specific edition

• ISBN is matched against edition identifiers
• ISBN normalization is applied
• Results are limited to selected library
Library-content searchText supports ISBN fields in the API. The mobile search experience is still required.
filter my books by format and reading status
I can focus on a subset of my collection

• Format filter works
• Reading-status filter works
• Filters can be combined with search
I can track my reading progress

• Unread, Reading, Read, OnHold and Abandoned are supported
• Change is saved to the specific copy
• Other copies are unaffected
I can remember where books are stored

• Location belongs to one library
• Copy can reference an optional location
• Parent/child locations are supported by the model
Location hierarchy and copy assignment exist in the model, but location management endpoints are missing.
edit the details of an owned copy
I can keep format, condition and notes accurate

• Format, reading status, condition, acquisition date, purchase price/currency, signed/favourite flags, location and notes can be updated
• Edition identity is not silently changed
• Unauthorized changes are rejected
remove a copy from my library
I can reflect books I no longer own

• Only targeted copy is removed
• Other copies of the edition remain
• Catalogue book/edition is not deleted as a side effect
browse a large library in pages

• API accepts pagination parameters
• Response includes page information
• Filtering and pagination work together
The library-content API supports pageNumber, pageSize, searchText, orderBy and orderDirection. Mobile paging and filtering controls are still required.
scan multiple ISBNs in one session
I can catalogue a large collection quickly

• Multiple scans are collected into a batch
• Items are visible before final import
• Scanning can continue without individual confirmation
I can catch mistakes and duplicates

• Batch lists found, duplicate and failed items
• User can exclude an item
• Confirmed batch is submitted for processing
import many editions as a batch
I can avoid repeating the add process

• Import batch and item records are persisted
• Each item has a processing outcome
• Successful items create copies in selected library
process large imports in the background
the app stays responsive during import

• Processing does not require an open request
• Batch status can be queried
• Individual item errors do not halt unrelated items
see a duplicate and failure summary after import
I know which books need attention

• Counts of imported, duplicate and failed items are shown
• Failures include actionable reasons
• Failed items can be reviewed
receive timely responses when a metadata provider is slow
a failed service does not freeze my lookup

• External requests have timeouts
• Transient errors use bounded retries
• Exhausted providers return a controlled error
Provider timeouts and fallback exist; bounded retry policies are not implemented.

• Redis caches appropriate lookup results
• Cache-aside lookup is implemented
• Cache failure does not prevent normal lookup

• Key request and import failures are logged
• Logs include correlation/context where appropriate
• Credentials and tokens are not logged
Metadata-provider failures are logged and API errors carry trace IDs; broader structured request/import logging is missing.

• Health endpoint is available
• Critical dependencies are checked appropriately
• Health response does not expose secrets
run unit tests for core business rules
changes do not break important behavior

• ISBN validation and duplicate states have tests
• Library access rules have tests
• Tests run repeatably
Implemented by repeatable unit tests for identity, libraries, ISBN lookup and ownership rules.
run integration tests for core API workflows
database and endpoint behavior is verified

• Auth and library API paths are tested
• ISBN lookup/import paths are tested
• Tests use isolated data

• API container builds successfully
• Required dependencies are configured
• Documented startup works on a clean machine

• CI runs on repository changes
• Build and tests run in pipeline
• Failures are visible
deploy the application to a production environment
the product can be used outside my development machine

• Production configuration is externalized
• Database migrations/deployment steps are documented
• API is reachable and health-checked
we can manage a shared collection

• Invitation targets an intended user
• Recipient can accept or decline
• Only authorized owner can invite
assign Owner, Editor or Viewer access

• Roles control read/write operations
• Viewer cannot modify books or copies
• Membership changes are authorized
Owner, Editor and Viewer roles are modeled and enforced; owner-facing membership assignment is missing.
choose who can see my library
I can protect or share my collection

• Visibility setting is stored
• Private and member-scoped access are respected
• Broader visibility modes follow configured permissions
Visibility is stored and editable; public, friends-only and broader visibility access rules are not implemented.
record that I lent a book copy
I can remember who has it

• Loan references a specific copy
• Borrower and loan date are recorded
• Active loan status is shown
record the return of a lent book

• Return date and status are updated
• Completed loan remains in history
• Duplicate return action is handled
save a book to my wishlist
I can remember books I want to buy

• Wishlist entry can reference desired book/edition
• Wishlist can be viewed and updated
• Wishlist entry is separate from owned copies
I can optionally share book interests

• Friend request can be sent
• Recipient can accept or reject
• Only permitted library information is visible
I can discover books they own

• Only libraries visible to the viewer are listed
• Private libraries are excluded
• Shared library access respects visibility and roles
identify a book without a readable barcode
I can still find its metadata

• User can submit book cover/text for recognition
• Recognized candidates require user confirmation
• Uncertain results can fall back to manual entry
I can use the app without a connection

• Previously synced data is available offline
• Offline state is clearly indicated
• Updates sync when connectivity returns
receive relevant library or loan notifications
I do not miss important updates

• Notification type and trigger are defined
• Only intended recipients receive messages
• Notification delivery failures are handled
update a library description and visibility

• Name, description and visibility support partial updates
• Empty descriptions can be cleared intentionally
• Invalid visibility values and unauthorized updates are rejected
list, search, sort and page through my libraries
I can find the collection I want to open

• Only libraries available to the current user are returned
• Search covers library name and description
• Paging metadata, stable sorting, role, member count and book count are returned
The paged/searchable/sortable library API is implemented. The mobile home/library-selection experience is still required.
author information can be corrected and completed

• Name, biography and life dates can be updated
• A death date before the birth date is rejected
• Unknown authors return a clear not-found response

• Publisher name and website can be updated
• Invalid URLs and empty requests are rejected
• Unknown publishers return a clear not-found response
update a book and its ordered authors
catalogue records can be corrected without duplicate author links

• Book metadata supports partial updates
• Author order is retained when associations change
• Unknown and duplicate author references are rejected
edition metadata and identifiers remain accurate

• Edition, publisher, ISBN, language, date, pages, cover and description can be updated
• ISBN checksums and related entity identifiers are validated
• Unknown editions return a clear not-found response
Backend implemented by PATCH /api/book-editions/{editionId}. The catalogue-editing UI is still required.
navigate books, authors, editions and publishers by relationship
I can explore the catalogue without duplicating data

• Books can be retrieved by author
• Authors and editions can be retrieved by book
• Publishers used by a book can be retrieved
Relationship and top-level catalogue GET endpoints are implemented. Frontend catalogue navigation is still required.
see metadata provenance and confirm web-search results
unverified metadata is not imported without review

• Lookup results identify their source and whether review is required
• Web-search metadata includes source references
• Import rejects review-required metadata without explicit confirmation
Metadata provenance, source URLs and confirmation enforcement are implemented in the API. The frontend review experience is still required.
import reviewed metadata atomically while reusing catalogue entities
concurrent or failed imports do not create partial duplicate data

• The ISBN is rechecked inside the transaction
• Existing authors, publishers and matching books are reused
• Book and edition changes commit together or roll back together
browse, search, sort and page through catalogue records
I can find books, authors, editions and publishers efficiently

• Books, authors, editions and publishers have list endpoints
• Results include paging metadata and deterministic sorting
• Search checks relevant text fields
• The frontend exposes browse, search, sort and paging controls
Backend list endpoints and common paging/search/sort parameters are implemented. Frontend catalogue browsing is still required.
view statistics about my reading and collection
I can understand my reading habits and collection composition

• Statistics are scoped to accessible libraries
• Counts and trends can be grouped by reading status and format
• Missing dates or optional metadata do not distort results
• The user can open the supporting books from a result
Identified in the README roadmap; no application workflow is implemented.
I can discover books that fit my interests without recommending books I already own

• Recommendations use permitted library or reading signals
• Already-owned books can be excluded
• The reason for a recommendation is understandable
• Recommendation processing respects privacy settings
Identified in the README roadmap; no recommendation workflow is implemented.
see loans that are due or overdue
I can follow up on books that have not been returned

• Active loans show borrower and expected return date
• Overdue status is derived consistently
• Returned and lost loans are distinguished
• Results include only copies the user may access
The loan model stores expected return dates and status, but loan-management endpoints and UI are not implemented.
